meaning: The comment states that the baseline mean flow q̄₀ is averaged over a 10 s window ending at BASELINE_T1 = 60 s, and that the volume integral is zeroed at 60 s rather than t = 0, so the start-up transient shows as a dip before the zero point instead of being folded into q̄₀. It also asserts specific onset times and a prior wrong result of -24 mL in M1 and M3.
expectation: Unknown in magnitude. Direction: every exported volume series is offset so it reads 0.000 mL at t = 60 s; any error in the window mean flow grows linearly with elapsed time over the rest of the run.

could_move.what: The quoted numbers (-24 mL in M1 and M3; onsets 340 s, 80 s, 117 s; ~1 s cardiac cycle) are prose claims, not read from code in this context. If scenario onsets change, the window can overlap a perturbation and stop being a baseline.
Zeroing at BASELINE_T1 instead of t=0 sets the offset of every exported volume series, so downstream plots and any volume-based residual inherit it.
The drift print in main() is the only stated check that the baseline is settled; its threshold and failure behaviour are not visible here.

check.why: Re-runs the export and its own drift print from t=60 s to each onset, showing whether the series reads 0.000 at 60 s and whether the window still ends before every onset, without refitting.
